A few days back, I got OG in @DlicomApp’s DC server. At the time when OG camping was going on, there wasn’t this much hype.

Recently I’ve been seeing a lot of discussion about it, so instead of just going with the hype, I properly did my own research.

There is a big centralization problem in social media + finance.

Right now, most platforms are controlled by big tech companies. Your data gets collected, conversations are moderated opaquely, ads use you but you don’t get fair rewards, and financial tools are often custodial or spread across different apps.

Privacy? Mostly secondary.
Ownership? Almost nothing.
The entire value flows upward to corporations, and the user becomes the “product.”

This is where @DlicomApp comes in.

They are building an all in one decentralized SocialFi ecosystem that gives control back to users — secure messaging, social networking, self-custody wallet, staking, in-chat transactions and more — all seamlessly integrated on a single platform.

Instead of using separate apps (one for chat, one for wallet, one for social), Dlicom combines everything into one privacy-first dApp built on blockchain (on scalable layers like Base and ZKsync).

In their model, users get:

• True data ownership and privacy (end-to-end encryption, no silent data harvesting)
• Self-custody wallet, manage assets, swaps, P2P payments
• Tokenized engagement earn through ads, staking rewards, and community activity via $DLI token
• Censorship resistance and decentralization, no single entity controlling everything
• AI assisted moderation, keeping things clean without big tech overreach

What is drawing attention:

– All in one hub: No need to switch apps for private chat, transactions and earning
– Strong focus on privacy + ownership in a world where AI and companies are heavily harvesting data
– Utility-driven tokenomics ($DLI powers fees, rewards and governance)
– Creator and community empowerment through tokenized interactions
– Early mover in seamless SocialFi + DeFi integration

Of course, nothing is 100% guaranteed — the project is still in building stage, presale/live ecosystem phase, and execution is very important.

But as social and finance continue to merge in Web3, platforms that solve real problems around privacy, ownership and unified experience can become big.

I am closely watching @DlicomApp. It will be important to see how it scales from here.

When Conversations Move Value: The Future of In-Chat Crypto with @DlicomApp 

Social platforms were built for conversation. Crypto was built for value transfer. The problem? They’ve rarely worked in the same place at the same time.

Dlicom flips that model by turning chat into a financial layer. Instead of forcing users to leave a thread to open a wallet and complete a transaction, value moves directly inside the conversation. Sending tokens feels no different than sending a message it happens in-line, in-context, and in real time.

At the center of the ecosystem is $DLI, an ERC-20 token designed for utility across messaging, tipping, staking, and governance. Its role isn’t just speculative, it’s functional. Activity on the platform feeds into a buyback and burn system funded by ad revenue and service fees, introducing deflationary mechanics tied to real usage.

The Stake for Revenue model, launched in Q2 2025, further aligns incentives. Holders can lock DLI and earn rewards based on platform performance, not just token emissions. Infrastructure-wise, Dlicom leverages Base for scalable throughput and integrates zero-knowledge proofs to protect user data while maintaining efficiency.

This gives rise to a unified experience where communication and digital value operate as one system not two separate apps competing for attention.

In an era where centralized social media platforms control user data, content visibility, and monetization, the need for a more user centric alternative is becoming increasingly clear. @DlicomApp positions itself as a Web3 based social platform that puts ownership of data, digital identity, and economic value back into the hands of users. This is not simply a traditional social app with crypto features added on, but an ecosystem designed from the ground up around decentralization and user ownership. Built with the idea that users should not be the product, Dlicom challenges the long standing Web2 model of platform control.

Dlicom combines social networking, encrypted communication, a non custodial crypto wallet, and DeFi functionality within a single application. Users can create posts, interact, send private messages, and make voice or video calls protected by end to end encryption. By relying less on centralized servers and more on decentralized infrastructure, the platform becomes more resistant to censorship while giving users greater authority over their content and interactions.

What truly sets Dlicom apart is the seamless integration of financial activity into social interaction. Its built in non custodial wallet allows users to manage digital assets, perform swaps, stake tokens, and even send crypto directly within chats. These activities are powered by the DLI utility token, which plays an active role in the platform’s internal economy, supporting incentives, access to features, and value exchange, rather than existing purely as a speculative asset.

Decentralization, however, also comes with responsibility. Blockchain transactions are irreversible, private keys must be secured by users themselves, and a basic understanding of Web3 concepts is essential. Yet this responsibility defines the shift Dlicom represents, a vision of the internet where social platforms are no longer owned by corporations, but by the people who use them. If Web2 was the era of platform owned networks, Web3 marks the rise of user owned ecosystems, and Dlicom together with @DlicomApp is positioning itself as part of that transition.

I want to discuss one topic today that we frequently overlook. We use financial services, messaging apps, and social media on a daily basis. However, if you examine further, you will notice that we have a number of structural issues.

1. Control
Data, algorithms, and account access are centralized. Users create digital identities, but do not fully own them.

2. Monetization of attention
User activity is converted into advertising revenue. The main economic benefit remains with the platform.

3. Centralized risk
When there is a single operator, there is a single point of control. Everyone is immediately impacted by any rule changes or technical malfunctions.

There is a solution to these problems. And that solution is @DlicomApp.

The first problem is control.
At Dlicom, this issue is solved through the integration of a self-custody wallet and decentralized social infrastructure. Users control their assets and interactions without intermediaries.

The second problem is monetizing attention.
Dlicom changes the platform's economy: part of the advertising revenue is distributed between users and creators, and the DLI token is used within the ecosystem for staking and internal settlements.

The third problem is centralized risk.
In Dlicom, key mechanisms operate through blockchain and smart contracts rather than through a single operator. This means that rules and financial processes do not depend on the decisions of a single company.

So we can confidently say that Dlicom is more than just an app. It’s a comprehensive ecosystem that combines communication, finance, and its own internal economy.

. @DlicomApp combines several different things: a social platform, messaging, and crypto tools. But today, I want to focus on one element in particular: the integrated crypto wallet.

If you look at how people interact online, many conversations sooner or later turn into transactions. Someone pays for a service, someone contributes to something, someone supports an author, or someone settles a debt.

Most services currently require you to exit the conversation, open another app, make the transfer, and then return.

But Dlicom makes this much more convenient. The wallet is built directly into the app, so transactions can happen while you're interacting. And this is where the main advantages of this approach appear.

The first is crypto transfers directly within the chat. During a conversation, you can immediately send cryptocurrency to the person you are chatting with.

The second is self-custody. The wallet does not function as a centralized balance in the platform’s database. The user controls their assets and keys. This is important because virtually the entire financial part of the platform is built on the user managing their own funds.

The third is the economic layer of the platform. The wallet is not only used to store assets. It also powers various economic mechanisms within the ecosystem: transfers between users, author support, internal payments, and other interactions related to the DLI token.

In addition, the Dlicom wallet has the classic capabilities of a Web3 environment. It allows asset management across several networks, token swaps through a liquidity aggregator, and access to decentralized applications using a built-in Web3 browser.

2030985858594087122.text:
. @DlicomApp is built on three key principles:

• Privacy
• Self-custody
• Decentralization

Each of them is responsible for a different part of how the platform works. In this post, I want to take a closer look at the first principle - privacy.

Privacy in Dlicom is not a single feature or tool. It consists of several layers of protection that work together within the platform architecture.

Simply put, there are three main levels of privacy:

1)  communication privacy
2)  asset privacy
3)  data privacy

The first level is communication privacy. 

Messages and calls on the platform are protected by end-to-end encryption. Only the participants in the conversation have access to its content.

No third party has access to these messages. In fact, this is the basic level of privacy for any platform where people communicate with each other.

The second level is asset privacy.

Dlicom uses a self-custody model. Users control their private keys themselves and, therefore, their crypto assets.

Funds are not stored on the platform. Asset management remains entirely with the wallet owner.

The third level is data privacy and the system architecture itself.

Dlicom uses a combination of on-chain and off-chain solutions. This approach helps maintain a balance between blockchain transparency, system performance, and user privacy.

Some data is processed through the blockchain infrastructure, which ensures data immutability. Media files can be stored on decentralized systems such as IPFS.

Today, I want to break down one important aspect of the @DlicomApp model. I’m talking about the 45% share of advertising revenue distributed among users. At first glance, this just looks like a large and attractive percentage. But if you look at the mechanics behind it, it becomes clear that there’s much more to it than that.

Modern social media platforms operate according to a simple model.

Users generate engagement, produce content, and increase traffic. Through advertising, the site makes money off of this interaction.

But the economic value generated by this activity remains almost entirely with the platform.

In the Dlicom model, a portion of advertising revenue is returned to those who generate activity on the platform.

These are content creators and users who interact with ads. In total, 45% of advertising revenue is distributed among these participants.

In other words, users now receive a portion of the economic value created by this activity in addition to generating traffic for the platform. To understand how it works in practice, it is enough to examine the fundamental logic of the system.

First, users create content and generate engagement within the platform. Advertisers pay for access to this engagement. After that, a portion of the advertising revenue is returned to the participants in the ecosystem.

Now it is important to understand what this model actually changes in the platform.

On traditional social networks, users generate activity, but the economic value of that activity remains almost entirely with the platform.

In the Dlicom model, part of that value is returned to those who create it.

User participation gains economic significance.

Activity, interaction with content, and viewing ads become elements of the reward system within the platform.

Advertising becomes part of the platform’s economy, not just a source of revenue.

Users, content creators, and advertisers interact within a single economic system.

And this is just a fraction of the changes this model brings about. But in practice, it affects a much broader structure of the platform, from the economic role of users and incentives for content creators to the way users, advertisers, and the platform itself interact.

2033634116424347912.text:
. @DlicomApp uses a staking model called SFR (Stake for Revenue).

Simply put, this means that users can stake DLI tokens and earn rewards generated from the platform’s revenue, rather than from newly minted tokens.

This method is not the same as staking in many cryptocurrency projects.

In most traditional staking systems, rewards are generated through the minting of new tokens. The protocol simply creates additional tokens and distributes them among stakers.

Because of that, the total supply keeps growing over time, which can put long-term inflation pressure on the token.

SFR is built differently.

In Dlicom, staking rewards come from the revenue the platform generates, not from printing new tokens. The platform earns revenue through things like advertising, platform services, and other on-chain activity. A part of that revenue is shared with users who stake DLI.

The mechanism itself is quite simple.

Users stake DLI tokens. These tokens remain locked for a selected period. When the platform generates revenue, a portion of that revenue is distributed among stakers in proportion to their stake.

This changes how staking works from an economic point of view.

Rewards are not coming from newly created tokens. They depend on the revenue the platform generates.

As the platform grows and more users start utilizing it, overall activity increases. That activity can generate more revenue, which can increase the rewards distributed to stakers.

Because of this, the growth of the platform directly affects staking rewards. When the ecosystem grows and more activity appears, the revenue behind those rewards grows as well. That means the platform and DLI holders benefit from the same thing: the development of the ecosystem.

Today, I want to look ahead and analyze how demand for DLI will form within @DlicomApp and where selling pressure will come from in this model.

Most tokens in the crypto space have utility. But the problem is that utility ≠ demand.

To put it another way, even if a token is required by the system, this does not ensure steady demand for it. And it often turns out that the price is sustained solely by new buyers.

To put it simply, it’s not about the token’s functions, but about how money flows through it.

And the key here is to understand where the demand actually comes from. I’ve broken it down into three types.

1) External demand

This is the most important factor. It refers to money entering the system from outside. In the case of Dlicom, this comes from advertising. Businesses pay for users’ attention. And this is where real demand for the token comes from.

2) Internal demand

This happens within the product:

- premium features
- gas fees
- payments between users

It exists, but on its own, it rarely drives the economy.

3) Speculative demand

The expectation that the token will rise in value. It is always present, but nothing stable can be built on it.

Now, on the other side is selling. Every token has sellers, and that's normal.

At Dlicom, it looks like this:

- users who receive rewards
- investors whose tokens are unlocking
- to some extent, stakers

And here’s the key point. The issue isn’t that someone is selling. The issue is who is buying and why.

When viewed as a whole, the issue is no longer just about demand or selling in isolation, but about how they are interconnected.

Value in:

- advertising budgets
- fees

Value out:

- user rewards
- staking rewards

And there is a third component: a portion of the revenue goes toward buying back and burning the token.

In other words, this is no longer just a token with functions. It’s a model where the token is directly linked to the flow of money within the platform.

And the key point here is that demand doesn’t exist on its own. It’s generated by real activity:

- product usage
- advertising budgets
- internal payments

That is precisely why Dlicom focuses not only on utility, but also on making sure the token is actually integrated into the platform’s real economy.

2035731175105294554.text:
Today I decided to compare @DlicomApp with various social networks specifically from the perspective of privacy.

To do this, I chose three different types of platforms:
Instagram - as a classic Web2 platform
Telegram - as a messaging app focused on privacy
Farcaster - as a Web3 social platform

And I’ll compare them with Dlicom to understand exactly how their approaches differ.

Next, I’ll break this down into several key aspects:
data control, message privacy, financial autonomy, and monetization model.

Data Control

These platforms differ in a very basic way when it comes to data control.

On Instagram, users have no control over their data at the infrastructure level. All information, including content and behavioral data, is stored and processed centrally. You use the service, but you have no influence over how the system works behind the scenes.

Telegram appears to be more private, but from a control perspective, it is also a centralized model. Data is stored on the company’s servers, and users effectively entrust the platform with its processing. Despite what the interface may suggest, this is not self-custody.

Farcaster is already moving toward Web3. Here, the user has more control over their identity and social graph. But the infrastructure is still not fully independent and depends on specific solutions and services.

Dlicom takes a different approach. Control over data is combined with blockchain architecture and a self-custody model. Users don’t just have an account; they interact with a system where data and assets aren’t tied to a single centralized entity.

Ultimately, the difference here is that in traditional platforms, control is a function of the service, whereas in Dlicom, it shifts to the user.

Messaging Privacy

Here, it’s important to look not only at whether private chats are available, but also at how they’re implemented.

On Instagram, messages are simply part of the product. They aren’t designed as a separate private layer and aren’t a key security feature.

Telegram is significantly stronger in this regard, but there are some nuances. Although it is accessible, not all chats have end-to-end encryption enabled by default. In other words, the level of privacy depends on how the user interacts with the product.

Farcaster isn’t focused on private messaging as a core feature. It’s more about public social interaction.

In Dlicom, communication is designed to be private from the very beginning. Encryption and data protection are built into the architecture, rather than added as a separate feature.

In Dlicom, privacy is an essential component of all communication, in contrast to other platforms where it is implemented partially or relies on particular features.

Financial Autonomy

Although it is closely related to privacy, this feature is frequently completely ignored in talks on privacy. Financial interaction also involves data, transactions, and control over assets. If a user does not control this aspect, their privacy remains incomplete.

Instagram does not have a financial layer as such. Any transactions, if they occur, take place outside the platform.

There are already financial tools available on Telegram, including TON-based wallets in its ecosystem, TON, and internal systems like Stars. However, these features remain a separate layer and are not fully integrated into the communication experience.

Farcaster provides access to the crypto ecosystem, but this is not part of the social experience itself.

In Dlicom, finance is integrated directly into communication. Instead of using additional services, users may manage assets and conduct transfers directly within the app.

Financial features are either completely absent or present separately on other platforms. In Dlicom, this is part of the core experience, so users can manage both their communication and their assets in one place.

Monetization and Data Usage

Another important point is how platforms handle the value created by users.

User data is the main resource in Instagram's business model. The platform monetizes attention and behavior, while users do not receive a direct share of the revenue.

Telegram has monetization tools, but they are more limited and are not built as a broad user revenue-sharing model across the platform.

Farcaster is currently experimenting with various models, but these are not yet stable or widely adopted.

In addition to rewarding activity and participation on the platform, users and creators receive a share of advertising revenue.

The difference lies not in the presence of monetization, but in its model. In Dlicom, the value created by users does not remain within the platform but is returned to them through rewards and participation.

To put it simply, on most platforms these features exist separately. In Dlicom, it’s all connected, and the user actually controls it.

Today, I want to discuss one important aspect of @DlicomApp: its infrastructure.

Most Web3 products are built on top of third-party networks. They consequently have no influence over fees, system behavior under stress, or performance.

At Dlicom, the approach is different.

The platform runs on its own infrastructure:
- private blockchain node
- EVM-compatible architecture
- support for multiple networks (Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, Optimism)

At the same time, Dlicom is developing its own Hyperchain (based on zkSync).

In the end, this is about control.
When you have your own infrastructure, you aren’t entirely dependent on third-party solutions or how they perform under load.

This is what makes scaling possible.
Dlicom combines a messenger, a social network, and payments. This is a rather demanding scenario that’s difficult to implement properly if the infrastructure is entirely external.

This directly affects fees and UX.
Less dependence on external networks means more opportunities to optimize costs and simplify interaction with the blockchain, including paying gas fees via DLI.

As a result, this isn’t just an app built on top of the blockchain. It’s an attempt to build its own infrastructure layer for the product and the economy within it.

Right now, apps like Instagram, WhatsApp are run by companies that own your data and can shut you out anytime.

Web3 is the idea that YOU should own your data, your money, and your identity, not a corporation.

Dlicom is built on that idea.

3. So what is Dlicom?
Dlicom is a SocialFi app : "Social" + "Finance" combined into one.

Think of it as: WhatsApp + Instagram + a crypto wallet + a browser - but decentralized, private, and you're in control.

Most people store crypto on exchanges (like Binance/Coinbase). Problem? They got hacked or If they go down, your funds could vanish.

@DlicomApp When Social Media Becomes a User-Owned Economy

Dlicom represents a new wave of Web3 social platforms aiming to merge everyday user behavior with on-chain value. 
Instead of reinventing social media from scratch, it retains familiar features such as feeds, short-form videos, messaging, and communities, while embedding financial ownership directly into the user experience. 
This approach lowers the entry barrier, allowing users to participate without needing deep blockchain knowledge.

At its core, Dlicom is built on a simple but powerful idea: users should benefit from the value they help create. Traditional platforms generate massive revenue from user activity, while users themselves capture very little of that value. 
By integrating tokens, staking mechanisms and direct tipping, Dlicom attempts to rebalance this system and turn participation into something economically meaningful.

One of its strongest advantages lies in product design. With a built-in non-custodial wallet, seamless in-app transactions and deployment on @base, the platform significantly reduces friction. Actions such as tipping or interacting with dApps feel as simple as using a Web2 application.

However, important challenges remain. The sustainability of its tokenomics and its ability to attract both creators and users will be key determining factors. Without strong network effects, even a well-designed product may struggle to scale.

Dlicom is not just a social application, but an experiment in transforming attention into ownership and participation into real economic value.

Dlicom – The Future of Decentralized Social Networking and Finance

@DlicomApp is a next-generation Web3-powered decentralized application (dApp) that combines social networking, digital finance, and secure communication into one unified ecosystem. Built with blockchain technology, it aims to give users full control over their data, identity, and digital assets while offering seamless interaction across communities and financial tools.

At its core, @DlicomApp is designed to move beyond traditional social media platforms by removing centralized control and replacing it with a user-owned, privacy-first digital environment.

What Dlicom Offers

Dlicom brings multiple services together in one platform:

1. Decentralized Social Media

Users can create posts, share content, and interact with communities without algorithmic manipulation or intrusive advertising. Content ownership stays with the user, promoting transparency and fairness. 

2. Secure Messaging & Communication

The platform includes end-to-end encrypted messaging, voice calls, and video calls, ensuring private and secure communication between users. 

3. Integrated Crypto Wallet

Dlicom provides a non-custodial wallet, allowing users to store, send, and receive cryptocurrencies directly within the app. It also supports in-app payments and gas fee management using its native token system. 

4. DeFi & Financial Tools

Users can access decentralized finance features such as staking, swapping, and token-based rewards. This enables users to earn passive income while participating in the ecosystem.

5. Decentralized Browser

Dlicom includes access to decentralized applications (dApps), allowing users to explore the broader Web3 ecosystem without leaving the platform.

DLI Token – The Ecosystem Fuel

The Dlicom ecosystem is powered by its native token DLI, which is used for:

Staking and rewards

In-app transactions and payments

Content tipping and monetization

Governance and ecosystem decisions

This creates a circular economy where user activity directly contributes to platform growth and rewards.

Dlicom is built around three major principles:

Privacy: Users control their data and identity

Ownership: Content and assets belong to users, not platforms

Decentralization: No central authority governs interaction or data flow

By combining these principles, Dlicom positions itself as more than a social app, it is an evolving Web3 digital ecosystem.

1. Single surface. Chat, posts, wallet, communities in one place. No app hopping, no context loss. Latency and UX matter for retention and they feel decent already
2. Self custody by default. Keys with you, end to end encrypted chat. Privacy without the usual convenience tax
3. Earn is a layer, not the loop. Activity creates assets, but the core loop is still talk and content. That is the right ordering
4. Community operations. Mods and contributors get roles and tools that map to real responsibilities and value flow. That is how you keep builders around

The fastest way to find product market fit is deployment first. Be in the field, talk to users inside the app, ship weekly, cut features that do not move retention. Replace vanity metrics with cohort stickiness. That is how robots got out of labs and it is how SocialFi gets out of hype

If $ETH rewards went to zero for a week would you still open Dlicom to talk to your circles

Right now I can jump into a room, move value with $USDC without leaving chat, and spin up a private group with custody intact. That baseline matters. The rest is execution and consistency

Platforms that win in this cycle will be product first communities where earn is a bonus, not the reason to show up. I want to see @DlicomApp keep deploying into real communities and publish retention and engagement over time. If they do, the upside is not airdrop games, it is a durable network effect owned by users

Web3 social platforms usually force a choice between self custody and usability. Users get a walled garden or a fragmented mess of wallet signatures. The recent architecture overhaul from @DlicomApp attempts to break that tradeoff.

The primary bottleneck for crypto social is context switching. Tipping historically meant leaving the feed and fighting with gas settings. Dlicom rebuilt their media player so tipping and sharing happen natively over the content. Actions now run at the speed of attention rather than block confirmations.

The infrastructure changes matter just as much. Crypto payments require a mental checklist of network states. This update handles EVM gas automatically behind the scenes. Wallet connections live entirely inside the ecosystem rather than booting users to external apps. It operates like a traditional application while retaining encrypted messaging on Base.

The hard part is user retention. Smooth transactions do not automatically guarantee network effects.

A few days ago, @DlicomApp released update 2.1.4.
This update removed many of the common Web3 inconveniences, including:

1. Fully redesigned DliClips experience
Previously, if you wanted to like, share, follow the creator, send them a tip, or report a clip, you had to switch between multiple screens several times. Now everything happens directly inside the clip with a single tap.

2. Smooth Transactions
One of the biggest pain points in Web3 is gas fees, network selection, transaction confirmations, and so on. Now most transfers happen with just one confirmation.

The system automatically handles gas on EVM chains thanks to its own Smart Contracts (Smooth Transactions + Meta Transactions). The user simply taps “Send” and gets an experience similar to regular fintech apps.

3. In-App Wallet Connect
Wallet connection now happens entirely inside Dlicom (as long as the wallet is already installed on the phone).

No more being redirected to another app, going back, and losing context. Connection takes just a few seconds, plus there’s now a toast notification.

4. Major performance improvements
The team carried out deep core optimization. Many key processes are now up to 5x faster.

The app now feels almost instant: scrolling, taps, loading - everything feels noticeably smoother on both iOS and Android.

So I’m glad to see Dlicom continuing to improve. I hope they keep the momentum going and build a truly high-quality product people genuinely want to use.

2059574569598370163.text:
Most creators in Web3 post consistently and still wonder why nothing compounds.

The problem is rarely effort. It's usually relevance.

Posting across too many unrelated topics kills the signal. The audience that came for one thing leaves when they get something else. Random content creates random audiences, and random audiences never turn into real communities.

The creators who actually build something own a clear angle. Not a rigid format, just a perspective that runs through everything they publish. People know exactly why they follow that account.

AI makes this more obvious, not less. It amplifies what's already there. When there's a clear identity, it helps that identity reach more people. When there's no identity, it just produces more noise.

Most creators already have their angle. They just haven't made it explicit yet. Look at your best content. Two or three recurring themes will show up. That's where the identity lives.

@DlicomApp published a full piece on this. Worth the read if you are building an audience right now

2059538708181741938.text:
Your audience doesn’t grow from volume. It grows from clarity.

A lot of creators in Web3 post every day, stay active, follow trends — but still feel like the audience never truly connects.

The problem usually isn’t consistency.
It’s relevance.

People follow creators when they clearly understand what they’re getting:
- a trader sharing real market reasoning
- a builder documenting the process
- a researcher finding angles others miss

Specificity matters.
Random content creates random audiences.
And random audiences rarely become real communities.
The strongest creators aren’t posting “everything.”
They own a perspective.
Strong positioning:
“People know why they follow me.”
Weak positioning:
“I just post whatever.”

That difference changes everything over time.
AI can amplify your reach, but it can’t replace identity. If there’s no clear angle behind the content, more output just becomes more noise.
Most creators already have their angle - they just haven’t defined it clearly yet.

A good question to ask yourself:
What topics do people consistently come back to me for?
Usually the answer is already hidden inside your best-performing posts.

That’s also why projects like @DlicomApp  stand out to me. They push creators not just to publish more, but to build recognizable identities and real long-term value inside communities. The advice and perspective shared there genuinely help creators think deeper about positioning instead of chasing empty metrics.
Know what you’re about.
Build around that.
Everything compounds from there.

And honestly - thank you for the advice. 🙏

The latest Dlicom update is probably the clearest sign yet that Web3 social apps are finally starting to feel… normal in the best possible way.

For a long time, simple actions inside crypto apps carried unnecessary friction. Tipping a creator meant opening extra menus. Connecting a wallet interrupted onboarding. Sending tokens often felt like filling out a form instead of making a payment.

This release quietly fixes a lot of that.

DliClips now feels far more native to how people actually consume content. You can like, share, follow, tip creators and report content directly from the clip itself without breaking the flow. Small change on paper, massive difference in actual usage.

The Smooth Transactions upgrade may be even more important. 
Gas handling and transaction complexity now happen mostly behind the scenes, turning supported transfers into a near one-tap experience. 
That shift matters because mainstream users do not want to think about network settings every time they send crypto.

The in-app wallet connection flow is another underrated improvement. 
Instead of bouncing users between multiple apps and confirmation screens, the process now stays inside Dlicom from start to finish, making onboarding feel much closer to a modern fintech app than a typical Web3 product.

Performance also got a serious overhaul. Faster loading, smoother scrolling, cleaner UI spacing, better notifications, improved audio behavior and fixes across multi-chain transfers all add up to an app that simply feels more polished day to day.

What stands out most is that many of these upgrades came directly from community feedback inside Discord. It feels less like a cosmetic update and more like Dlicom refining the core experience around how people actually use the product.

And apparently, the next release is already in build.

Web3 apps are entering the phase where user experience matters just as much as infrastructure. Updates like this are a reminder that adoption often comes down to removing friction one tap at a time.

Most crypto communication is optimized for visibility, not understanding.

That is the core inefficiency @DlicomApp seems to be targeting, and it is more important than it looks at first glance.

⸻

Information is not the problem. Structure is.

In Web3, projects rarely suffer from lack of content.

They suffer from lack of coherence.

A single update might appear on X, get expanded in Telegram, summarized in Medium, clipped into a video, and partially discussed in community threads.

Each piece is technically “available,” but none of it forms a complete, stable narrative.

The result is simple: users see activity, but not clarity.

⸻

Dlicom as a coordination layer

Dlicom’s direction can be understood as an attempt to coordinate how information flows across fragmented platforms.

Instead of treating social channels as separate audiences, it leans toward treating them as synchronized surfaces of a single communication system.

The value is not in adding more content channels.

It is in aligning them so that information maintains consistency, timing, and context regardless of where it is consumed.

This shifts the focus from broadcasting to structuring.

⸻

Why this matters at scale

As ecosystems grow, communication overhead increases faster than technical complexity.

Even strong projects begin to degrade in user experience because:

updates lose context as they spread
community narratives diverge across platforms
onboarding becomes dependent on insider knowledge

If Dlicom’s approach works, it addresses a hidden bottleneck in Web3 growth: cognitive fragmentation.

Not scalability of infrastructure, but scalability of understanding.

⸻

Perspective

What is interesting here is the reframing of “community management” into something closer to information architecture.

Most projects invest in building stronger messages.

This approach assumes the issue is not message strength, but message integrity across distribution paths.

That is a quieter problem, but a more foundational one.

⸻

If Web3 is moving toward larger, more interconnected ecosystems, then coordination of information may become as critical as coordination of transactions.

Dlicom is essentially betting on that shift.

◆ identity remains connected to users

Posts, conversations, replies, communities, and constant interaction are what keep digital platforms alive and growing every day.

But while users generate the activity,

platforms usually capture most of the long-term value created from that attention.

People spend hours:

◈ sharing ideas
◈ interacting with communities
◈ creating discussions
◈ helping networks grow

yet ownership over that activity rarely stays with the users themselves.

That dynamic shaped much of the modern internet economy.

@DlicomApp is building toward a more user-centered model where messaging, participation, identity, and value creation exist closer to the community layer rather than remaining fully controlled by centralized platforms.

That shift feels increasingly important because online interaction itself is becoming economically valuable infrastructure.

Digital communities are no longer functioning as simple social spaces.

They are gradually becoming:

▹ coordination networks
▹ ownership-driven ecosystems
▹ digital economies built around participation

As SocialFi infrastructure continues evolving, platforms combining communication with user ownership may fundamentally reshape how people interact, contribute, and capture value across the internet.

Most crypto projects don’t fail because they are building the wrong thing. They fail because nobody can clearly understand what they are doing at the right time.

That sounds simple, but it is actually one of the biggest hidden problems in Web3 today. Information is everywhere, yet clarity is rare. Updates drop on X, deeper explanations sit on Medium, discussions move to Telegram, clips appear on YouTube, and reactions spread across Reddit and other communities. Each platform holds a piece of the truth, but rarely the full picture.

The result is not a lack of communication. It is fragmentation of meaning.

Dlicom positions itself around this exact gap. Instead of treating social platforms as separate channels that need constant posting, it leans toward something more structured: coordination of information across platforms so that the same message does not lose context as it moves. The focus shifts away from volume and toward alignment.

In practice, this means communication is not just about broadcasting updates. It is about ensuring that every surface where a user interacts with a project reflects the same narrative, timing, and intent. The goal is to reduce the mental effort required for users to piece things together on their own.

This matters more as ecosystems grow. Early-stage projects can survive messy communication because the scope is small and communities are tight. But as adoption scales, the cost of fragmented messaging increases. New users struggle to onboard, long-term users miss context, and community understanding slowly drifts in different directions. Over time, this creates friction that is not technical, but cognitive.

What stands out about Dlicom’s approach is that it treats communication as infrastructure rather than marketing. Most teams try to improve messaging by making it louder or more frequent. This direction suggests something different: the problem is not lack of communication, but lack of coherence across distribution.

If that assumption is correct, then the real challenge in Web3 is not just scaling systems or communities, but scaling shared understanding without losing consistency. That is a harder problem than most people give it credit for.

Dlicom is essentially betting that the next phase of crypto growth will depend not only on better technology, but on better coordination of information itself. And if that turns out to be true, then communication structure becomes just as important as protocol design.

It is not a flashy problem. But it is a foundational one.
@DlicomApp

2062090258083201505.text:
The next major challenge for Web3 may not be scalability.

It may be attention.

For years, the industry has focused on building faster blockchains, better infrastructure, and more sophisticated financial systems. Yet one problem continues to quietly slow adoption: information fragmentation.

Every day, communities are flooded with updates. Announcements appear on X. Discussions happen on Telegram. Long-form insights are published on Medium. Videos are uploaded to YouTube. Conversations spread across Reddit and countless other channels.

The information exists.

The understanding often does not.

This is what makes Dlicom an interesting project to watch.

Rather than approaching growth through speculation or short-term engagement tactics, Dlicom appears to be focused on something more fundamental: improving how information moves between projects and communities.

The importance of this should not be underestimated.

In traditional technology, successful platforms are often built on efficient information flow. Search engines organize information. Social networks distribute information. Communication platforms connect information.

Web3, despite its technological progress, still struggles with information coordination.

Base: Coinbase’s Layer 2 Blockchain Revolutionizing Web3
And Why Dlicom Stands to Gain Massively by Building on It

1. What is Base?

Base is a Layer 2 (L2) blockchain built on Ethereum by Coinbase, one of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges. Launched in 2023, it uses the OP Stack (Optimism’s technology) to deliver a scalable, secure, and extremely affordable experience while inheriting Ethereum’s security.Unlike Ethereum mainnet (Layer 1), where gas fees can skyrocket during congestion, Base processes most transactions off-chain, batches them, and settles them on Ethereum. The result: very low fees (often 5–20x cheaper than Ethereum), high speed, and full compatibility with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM).

2.Key Features of Base:

Security: Inherits Ethereum’s security through Optimistic Rollups.

Ultra-low cost: Transactions often cost just a few cents.

High scalability: Handles thousands of transactions per second (TPS).

Developer-friendly: Ethereum smart contracts deploy with minimal changes.

Coinbase integration: Seamless access to millions of Coinbase Wallet users and onchain products.

Fast-growing ecosystem: DeFi, SocialFi, NFTs, gaming — Base has become one of the most vibrant L2s.

Base’s mission is to onboard the next billion users to Web3 by making crypto as simple and affordable as traditional apps.

3. Dlicom: An AI-Powered SocialFi Project Natively Built on Base

Dlicom ($DLI) is a SocialFi platform that combines a decentralized social network, end-to-end encrypted messaging, a self-custody multi-chain wallet, and creator monetization tools (on-chain tipping, etc.). Powered by AI and built natively on Base, the project is currently in presale with $DLI as its ERC-20 token

4.Key Advantages for Dlicom by Building on Base

Microscopic Fees = Viable Micro-Transactions
On a social platform, users want to tip creators $0.10, vote, or send frequent payments without paying $5 in gas. Base makes this economically viable. Tipping, staking rewards, and daily interactions become smooth and attractive to mainstream users.

Full EVM Compatibility & Easy Development
The Dlicom team can reuse all existing Ethereum tools (Solidity, Hardhat, etc.) without learning a new stack. Faster deployment, simpler audits, and easy integration with other DeFi protocols on Base.

Direct Access to Coinbase’s Massive User Base
Coinbase has tens of millions of users. Base is deeply integrated with Coinbase Wallet. Dlicom gains huge distribution potential and simplified onboarding for non-crypto users coming through Coinbase.

Scalability for Mass Adoption
A social app can generate millions of interactions daily (posts, likes, messages, tips). Base handles this load without congestion or high fees — unlike Ethereum L1 or some other chains.

Institutional-Grade Security & Trust
Being on Base (built by Coinbase) builds user and investor confidence. Security is backed by Ethereum, and Coinbase adds strong regulatory and technical credibility.

Lower Costs = Higher Ecosystem Value
Cheaper fees lead to more active users, higher transaction volume, and greater value accrual for the $DLI token through staking, governance, and in-app utility.
Positioned in a High-Growth L2

Base is attracting many SocialFi and DeFi projects. Dlicom benefits from network effects: liquidity, tools, partnerships, and users already present on the chain.

Conclusion: A Strategic Winning 

ChoiceBy building on Base, Dlicom isn’t just choosing a blockchain — it’s choosing the infrastructure best suited for mainstream consumer applications: fast, cheap, secure, and connected to the Coinbase giant.For a SocialFi project focused on daily monetization, privacy, and massive adoption, Base offers the perfect balance of performance, cost, and distribution.

2063180548810391885.text:
Why Visual Content Matters on Dlicom

One thing I've noticed while spending time on @DlicomApp  is how much first impressions matter.

Before anyone reads a caption, joins a discussion, or reacts to a post, they see the visual. A single image, a short clip, a screenshot, or even a simple graphic can be the difference between someone scrolling past and someone stopping to engage.

What I like about Dlicom is that it gives everyone the opportunity to build an audience, regardless of their experience or resources. You don't need expensive software, a design team, or professional equipment. What matters most is creating content that resonates with people.

This is especially true with DliClips. Short-form vertical video has become one of the most effective ways to reach new audiences, and the barrier to entry is lower than many people think. A clear idea and a strong hook in the first few seconds can outperform highly produced content.

The creators who stand out on Dlicom aren't necessarily the ones with the most polished visuals. They're the ones who understand their communities and use visuals to start conversations.

That's what makes the platform interesting to me. The best visuals don't just decorate content-they communicate something on their own. They make people stop, pay attention, and engage.

As Dlicom continues to grow, I think visual storytelling will play an even bigger role in helping creators connect with their audiences and build meaningful communities.

Part 3: SFR Mechanism | Staking for Revenue
One thing worth looking at in @DlicomApp is the SFR mechanism.

Most social platforms generate value from user activity, but users rarely see that value return to them in a clear way.

SFR takes a different approach by connecting staking with the revenue side of the ecosystem.

So the token is not only about holding or trading. It becomes part of how users participate in the platform’s value flow.

To me, this matters for SocialFi.

Content and community can bring users in, but long-term retention needs stronger alignment.

If Dlicom can make staking, usage, and revenue work together in a simple way, SFR could become one of the more important pieces of the model.

@dlicom_vn

2062111459975610442.text:
Part 4: App v2.1.0 & User Experience

For any Web3 social app, the product experience matters more than the narrative.

People may come for the idea, but they only stay if the app feels simple enough to use every day.

That is why App v2.1.0 is an important part to watch for @DlicomApp.

The direction seems clear: make Web3 feel closer to a normal social experience.

Users should be able to explore content, chat, join communities, manage their wallet, and access Web3 tools without constantly switching between different apps.

To me, this is where Dlicom becomes more practical.

If the product can reduce friction while keeping ownership and value flow in the background, then SocialFi becomes easier for real users to understand.

Good UX is not just about looking smooth.

It is about making complicated things feel natural.

@dlicom_vn

2062597158231232663.text:
Part 5: Tokenomics & Presale

For any Web3 project, tokenomics is not just about numbers.

It shows how the ecosystem is designed to grow.

With @DlicomApp , the key point is whether the token can support real activity inside the social layer.

Not just holding or trading, but utility around users, creators, staking, rewards, and ecosystem participation.

The presale also matters because this is where early conviction starts to form.

To me, strong tokenomics should create alignment.

If users, creators, stakers, and the platform can grow in the same direction, the token becomes part of the product, not just a separate asset.

That is the angle I’m watching with Dlicom.

@dlicom_vn

Most creators think growth comes from posting more.

Create content that your audience can relate to.
Share ideas that spark curiosity.
Use visuals that support your message instead of distracting from it.

A simple image with a strong message can outperform a perfect design with no meaning behind it.

Focus on value.
Focus on consistency.
Focus on creating something people want to share.

A few days ago, someone said something to me that I haven’t really been able to shake off:

“Do something meaningful with your life.”

At first, I brushed it off.

But later that night, after work, it came back to me.

Because from the outside, it’s easy for all of that to look like noise.

You start wondering if you’re actually moving forward or simply keeping yourself busy.

I think a lot of people in Web3 have had that thought before.

Especially when progress feels slow.

When life is demanding your attention. When other people seem to be moving faster. When the results you hoped for haven’t shown up yet.

But the more I sat with that question, the more I realized something.

Meaningful work rarely feels meaningful in the moment.

Most of the time, it looks like learning. It looks like consistency. It looks like showing up before anyone notices.

That’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about being part of @DlicomApp

The longer I’m here, the less it feels like I’m chasing rewards and the more it feels like I’m building skills, relationships, and experiences I’ll carry with me long after any campaign ends.

Maybe that’s not the whole destination.

But it’s definitely not nothing.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐚𝐩𝐩 𝐈 𝐰𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐝 𝐞𝐱𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐥𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐲 𝐞𝐱𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝, 𝐈 𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐩𝐚𝐲𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

They solve the problems you've stopped noticing.

The biggest barrier to Web3 isn't technology.

It's complexity.
Most people don't leave Web2 because they don't understand blockchain.

They leave because the onboarding experience is painful.

Create a wallet. Save a seed phrase. Switch networks. Pay gas fees.

The most expensive products on the internet are often the ones that appear free.

Social media is the perfect example.

You don't pay with money.

You pay with data.

Every click.
Every like.
Every comment.
Every second of attention.
It's all collected, analyzed, and monetized.
The business model of Web2 isn't built around users.
It's built around user data.

The more time you spend on a platform, the more valuable you become to advertisers.

Think about it:

Billions of people create content for free.
Generate engagement for free.
Provide data for free.

Yet the economic value flows elsewhere.

Users produce the asset.

Platforms own the asset.
That's the hidden cost of "free."
Not because social media is evil.

But because the incentives are misaligned.

When your data is the product, your interests are rarely the priority.

This is where SocialFi introduces a different model.

Instead of extracting value from users,
it creates mechanisms for users to participate in the value they create.

Ownership.
Monetization.
Self-custody.
Privacy.

Not as features.

As principles.

The next evolution of social media isn't about better algorithms.

It's about better alignment.
Because the people creating the value should have a stake in it.

@DlicomApp

Dlicom: The Quiet Architecture of a New Internet — Where SocialFi, AI, and Self-Custody Finally Meet on Base

A long-form look at how Dlicom is rebuilding social communication for the on-chain era.

A new signal in a noisy world
Every decade or so, the internet rearranges itself. The early web gave us pages. Web2 gave us platforms. Each shift quietly redefined who owns the conversation — and who profits from it.

We are now standing inside the next rearrangement, and it doesn't look like another app store launch or a louder feed. It looks like a fundamental rewrite of the relationship between users, creators, and the platforms they live on. Identity is becoming portable. Wallets are becoming social. Messages are becoming assets. AI is becoming a co-pilot, not a surveillance layer.

In the middle of this shift, a project called Dlicom is building something that feels less like a product and more like a thesis: that social, financial, and AI experiences should live in one self-custodied space, owned by the people who use it.

This is the story of that thesis and why it matters.

extracting from it.
The result is a platform where opening a chat, watching a clip, joining a community, or tipping a creator are all parts of the same continuous on-chain motion  no app-switching, no broken context, no custodial middleman holding the keys.

Inside the Dlicom ecosystem
Dlicom isn’t a single feature dressed up as a platform. It’s a small ecosystem with several connected surfaces, each designed to remove a friction point from on-chain life.

Self-custody wallet at the core
Everything in Dlicom starts at the wallet. It's a non-custodial wallet, meaning the keys live with the user — not on a company's server. From this single wallet, users can hold assets, sign transactions, interact with dApps, stake, and authenticate across the rest of the Dlicom experience.

The wallet isn't a separate tab to remember. It's the identity layer behind every action: every chat, every clip, every post.

2. Encrypted messaging

Private conversations on Dlicom are designed around end-to-end encryption, not metadata harvesting. The point isn't only privacy in the abstract — it's that chat becomes a financial surface. Once a conversation is encrypted and tied to a self-custody wallet, in-chat transactions stop feeling like a bolt-on and start feeling like the natural shape of messaging.

You can talk to a friend, send them tokens, split a payment, or settle a creator tip — all inside the same encrypted thread, without exposing keys or routing through a third party.

3. The Web3 browser

A native Web3 browser turns Dlicom into more than a single app — it becomes a doorway to the wider on-chain world. Users can explore decentralized applications, connect to protocols, and interact with smart contracts using the same wallet identity they already have inside Dlicom.

This matters because Web3's biggest UX failure is fragmentation. Wallets, browsers, dApps, and chats rarely speak the same language. Dlicom's browser collapses those layers into one continuous session.

4. DliClips   short-form video, on-chain native

DliClips is Dlicom's short-form video layer — the cultural front door of the platform. If TikTok and Reels showed how powerful vertical video can be, DliClips reframes that format under a different economic logic.

Creators on DliClips own their content and their audience. Engagement isn't just a vanity metric flowing into a platform's ad business; it's a signal that can be tied directly to creator rewards, community participation, and on-chain reputation. The format is familiar. The ownership model is not.

5. SocialFi-native feed and communities

Around the wallet, chat, browser, and clips sits the social layer: feeds, communities, and creator spaces designed for participation, not extraction. Posting, commenting, and following are not just engagement loops   they are the substrate for a healthier creator economy where attention is rewarded transparently.

Why Your Wallet Matters More Than Ever in SocialFi

When people think about SocialFi, they often focus on content, followers, and engagement. But behind every interaction is something equally important: your wallet.

A wallet is more than a place to store digital assets. It is your identity, your access point, and your ownership layer in the Web3 ecosystem.

With the Dlicom Wallet, users can manage their assets while staying connected to their communities. Instead of relying on centralized platforms, you maintain control over your funds and digital presence.

Ownership Changes Everything

Traditional social platforms allow you to create content, but they own the infrastructure. In Web3, your wallet gives you direct ownership of assets, rewards, and on-chain activity.

Every transaction, reward, and interaction becomes part of a transparent ecosystem where users have greater control.

Security and Self-Custody

One of the biggest advantages of a self-custody wallet is that you control your private keys. This means your assets remain under your control, not held by a third party.

With great control comes responsibility, which is why protecting your recovery phrase and practicing good security habits is essential.

A Gateway to Web3

A wallet is not just for sending and receiving tokens. It unlocks access to decentralized applications, creator economies, community rewards, and new opportunities across the blockchain ecosystem.

As SocialFi continues to evolve, wallets will become the foundation that connects identity, reputation, and value.

The Future Is User-Owned

The next generation of social platforms is built around ownership and participation. Dlicom Wallet helps users move beyond being passive consumers and become active participants in the digital economy.

In Web3, your wallet isn't just a tool.

It's your key to the future.

Why The Future Of Social Media Is Bigger Than Content

Social media was built to help people connect.

Web3 is helping people own what they create.

For years, users have been forced to split their digital lives across multiple platforms.

One app for communication.

Another for payments.

Another for creator earnings.

Another for crypto and digital assets.

The result?

A fragmented experience that slows participation and limits opportunity.

Dlicom takes a different approach.

It combines social networking, encrypted messaging, creator monetization, self-custody wallets, staking, and Web3 access into a single mobile ecosystem.

The significance goes beyond convenience.

Online communities are evolving into digital economies where users want more than likes and followers.

They want:

• Ownership of their digital presence
• Direct monetization opportunities
• Greater community influence
• Financial participation
• Control over their assets and identity

As Web3 adoption grows, platforms that merge social interaction with economic participation may define the next era of the internet.

Dlicom is building with that future in mind.

Why Creator Monetization Needs An Upgrade

For years, creators have depended on advertising revenue, sponsorships, and platform algorithms.
The problem is simple.
Creators generate value but often have limited control over how they earn from it.
A single algorithm change can reduce visibility overnight.
A payment provider can create restrictions.
A platform can change monetization policies without notice.

This is why direct value transfer is becoming increasingly important.
@DlicomApp introduces EVM-based tipping, allowing creators to receive support directly from their audience.
No complex intermediaries.

No waiting weeks for payouts.
No dependence on advertising alone.
As digital communities continue expanding, creator economies may increasingly move toward direct participation models.

The strongest creator ecosystems of the future could be those where value moves freely between creators and communities.
Dlicom is helping explore that direction.

​Most servers have a specific channel for new members. Look for channels named #rules, #welcome, #read-me, or #roles.

​Read the instructions carefully.

​Often, you just need to react to a message (click an emoji below a post) to automatically get the role.

​2. Look for an #apply-here or #support Ticket

​If the "Deliver" role is an official job or staff position (like a delivery rider, courier, or server uploader):

​Look for an #apply or #application channel.

​Check if there is a Ticket System (a channel where you click a button to open a private chat with the admins) to request the role.

​3. Use Bot Commands

​Some servers use bots to assign roles. Check if there is a channel named #bot-commands or #verify. You might need to type a command like /role or !join.

​4. Ask the Staff / Admins

​If you cannot find any instructions:

​Go to the #general-chat or #help channel.

Been digging into @DlicomApp for the last few hours. Here's what I found.

It's an AI-powered SocialFi app on @base. Features include encrypted messaging & calls, personalized feed, DliClips, self-custody wallet, Web3 browser, and on-chain creator tipping. They have a cute mascot called Dili.

The app is already live on GooglePlay and AppStore. That's one thing I like they actually built the product first instead of just launching a token.

Now the token part. $DLI is on Base. Currently in presale. They've raised $3.32M so far out of $12.42M target. Price is $0.05. FDV sitting around $17-18M range.

The main utility they're pushing is SFR Stake For Revenue. You stake $DLI and supposedly earn $USDT from actual platform revenue (tipping, premium features, etc). It's interesting on paper.

They also got a Hacken audit done back in Feb 2026. That's a plus.

Community is very active, especially from Bangladesh and Southeast Asia. Lots of Discord tasks, referrals, and points farming going on. The official account posts a lot of lighthearted Dili content.

But here's the thing farming activity is quite heavy. A lot of the engagement looks coordinated. That's pretty common in these kinds of projects though.

No major scam or rug accusations popped up in my search, which is good. Still, it's pre-TGE, so a lot of things are unproven right now.

Overall, product looks decent and they’re being somewhat transparent about the presale numbers. But like most SocialFi projects, execution after token launch will decide everything.

Would I ape in right now? Probably not without seeing the full tokenomics and how the revenue share actually works post-launch.

Just sharing what I found. DYOR as always.

@DlicomApp SocialFi: The Future of Decentralized Social Networking

In a digital world where privacy is becoming increasingly important and users are demanding more control over their data, @DlicomApp is building a next-generation SocialFi ecosystem that combines social networking, AI, blockchain, and Web3 technology into a single powerful platform.

Unlike traditional social media platforms that monetize user data and control content distribution, Dlicom focuses on user ownership, privacy, and creator
 empowerment. The platform aims to create a decentralized social environment where users can communicate, create, and earn without sacrificing control over their digital identity.
Key Features of Dlicom

 AI-Powered Social Experience Dlicom leverages artificial intelligence to provide personalized content recommendations and improve user engagement while maintaining user privacy.

 Encrypted Messaging & Calls Security is one of the project's core priorities. Users can enjoy encrypted messaging and calling features designed to protect personal conversations from unauthorized access.

 DliClips Content Platform Creators can share short-form content and engage with their communities through DliClips, helping users discover new content while giving creators additional exposure.

 Self-Custody Wallet Unlike centralized platforms, Dlicom integrates a self-custody wallet, allowing users to maintain full ownership and control over their digital assets and cryptocurrencies.

Built-In Web3 Browser The platform includes a Web3 browser that enables seamless interaction with decentralized applications, making blockchain adoption easier for everyday users.

 On-Chain Creator Tipping Content creators can receive direct blockchain-based support from their audiences through transparent on-chain tipping mechanisms, creating new monetization opportunities.

Why Dlicom Stands Out
The SocialFi sector continues to grow as users seek alternatives to traditional social media platforms. Dlicom is positioning itself at the intersection of SocialFi, AI, and Web3 by creating an ecosystem where users are not just participants but stakeholders.

The project's rapid community growth demonstrates increasing interest in decentralized social platforms. Reaching over 20,000 Discord members highlights the strong engagement and belief that the community has in the vision Dlicom is building.

The Bigger Vision

Dlicom is not simply creating another social media application. The team is working toward a future where communication, content creation, digital ownership, and financial incentives coexist within a decentralized ecosystem.

As Web3 adoption accelerates, projects like Dlicom have the potential to redefine how people connect online by giving users ownership of their identity, content, and value creation.

The future of social networking may not belong to centralized platforms it may belong to communities. And Dlicom is working to be one of the projects leading that transformation.

Privacy & ZK Technology: How Dlicom Approaches On-Chain Social

When I first started exploring SocialFi as a space worth covering seriously, the conversation was almost always dominated by token incentives, follower monetization, and on-chain reputation  but rarely the one thing that actually determines whether mainstream users will ever migrate from Web2 to Web3 social platforms: privacy, and I think Dlicom is one of the first protocols to genuinely confront that gap head-on rather than paper over it with marketing language. What Dlicom is building isn't just another decentralized social graph  it's an architecture that treats privacy as a first-class protocol primitive, embedding encryption and Zero Knowledge proofs directly into the social layer itself, which fundamentally changes what it means to "post" or "message" on-chain, because right now the uncomfortable truth about most SocialFi platforms is that transparency the very thing that makes blockchain trustworthy  becomes a liability the moment you're talking about private conversations, personal relationships, or sensitive community discussions, and Dlicom resolves that tension by leveraging ZK technology to allow users to prove that an interaction happened, that a message was delivered, that a credential is valid, all without ever exposing the actual content of that interaction to the public chain, which is exactly how privacy should work in a decentralized context. What makes this approach particularly compelling to me is the self-custody wallet architecture  Dlicom integrates the wallet natively into the application itself rather than treating it as an external tool you connect from MetaMask or Phantom, meaning the user's keys, their identity, their data sovereignty, all live within a unified experience that doesn't require them to understand seed phrases before they can send a message, and that UX decision alone is significant because it removes the single biggest friction point that has historically prevented non-crypto-native users from engaging with on-chain social tools, while simultaneously keeping the self-custody philosophy intact, so you're not trading decentralization for convenience you're getting both. The ZK proof mechanism Dlicom deploys is especially worth unpacking because it enables something that Telegram and Discord structurally cannot offer: verifiable interactions without surveillance, meaning a user can prove they're a member of a group, prove they've completed an on-chain action, or prove their identity credentials without leaking metadata to the platform operator, advertisers, or government actors, and given what we've seen with Telegram's legal entanglements and Discord's centralized data vulnerabilities, that's not a niche concern — it's a civilizational-scale problem that ZK cryptography is uniquely positioned to solve. So when I ask myself whether ZK-powered social networks can realistically replace Telegram and Discord, my honest answer is that the question isn't really about capability anymore  the cryptography is mature enough, the infrastructure is improving rapidly, and protocols like Dlicom are proving that the UX can be streamlined  the real question is adoption velocity, because replacing deeply entrenched communication tools requires not just technical superiority but a triggering event, whether that's a regulatory crackdown, a data breach, or a cultural shift toward privacy consciousness, and I believe we're closer to that inflection point than most people realize, which is precisely why I think Dlicom's architectural decisions today position it as one of the most strategically significant social protocols being built in this cycle.@DlicomApp #DLICOM #Web3 #CryptoCommunity

Web3 social platforms have been promising to revolutionize the creator economy for years, but most suffer from clunky UX and fragmented wallet connections.
Enter **Dlicom** — the Web3 SocialFi app that is quietly becoming a massive magnet for devs and creators.
Here is a breakdown of why builders are migrating to Dlicom and why its creator-to-user ratio is currently crushing traditional platforms (🧵👇):
### 1. The Frictionless Native Wallet
The biggest drop-off in Web3 apps happens at the "Connect Wallet" stage. If users have to leave an app to sign a transaction, they bounce.
Dlicom completely eliminates this. Every account comes with a **built-in, self-custody EVM wallet** from signup. No third-party custody, no app switching. For devs, this means a massive spike in user retention because the entire flow happens natively.
### 2. Direct Onchain Monetization
Traditional platforms optimize for algorithmic visibility; Dlicom optimizes for interaction and ownership.
Through the main social feed and their short-form video feature (**DliClips**), audiences can send EVM-based tips *directly* to creators. No middlemen, no waiting for payouts, no arbitrary demonetization. Your wallet identity is tied directly to your presence.
### 3. A Built-In Web3 Browser (A Dev's Dream)
This is where it gets highly lucrative for developers. Dlicom features a built-in dApp browser. Users can access decentralized applications and Web3 protocols without ever leaving their social ecosystem. If you are building a dApp, Dlicom provides a captive, Web3-native audience ready to interact directly through their built-in wallets.
### 4. End-to-End Encrypted Privacy
While most social apps harvest your data, Dlicom locks it down. Every private conversation on the platform is end-to-end encrypted. Combined with self-custody of your private keys, it actually respects the core ethos of Web3: *Your keys, your data, your control.*
### 5. Communities Built on Meaningful Reputation
Instead of shallow activity loops and bot farming, Dlicom’s architecture focuses on long-term community relationships. They give admins real moderation controls to curate culture and quality. Trust is built through observable behavior over time, making it a much healthier ecosystem for genuine engagement.
**The Takeaway:**
Social platforms are becoming economic infrastructure. Reputation, behavior, and capital are flowing through social layers, but users rarely own the value they create. Dlicom is flipping the script by making social infrastructure completely centered around *ownership*.
If you are a Web3 dev, creator, or just someone tired of rented audiences, it's time to claim your identity.

And honestly?

Low fees

Transactions confirm in seconds. Social apps need to feel instant.

Coinbase backing
Institutional credibility plus a massive existing user ecosystem from day one.

Millions already on Base
Dlicom is not starting from zero. The audience is already here.

THE BIGGER PICTURE

Web2 social apps run on centralized servers owned by one company. One decision can take everything down.

2061972496270925896.text:
Open WhatsApp. Go to settings. Find privacy. Enable encryption.

Why is privacy something you have to turn on?

On Dlicom, it is on before you even open the app.

WHAT IS END-TO-END ENCRYPTION?

When a message is end-to-end encrypted, only the sender and the receiver can read it.

Not the platform. Not the servers. Not the government. Nobody else.

The message is locked on your device and unlocked only on your recipient's device.

HOW OTHER APPS HANDLE THIS

Telegram: encryption is off by default. You have to manually start a "Secret Chat."

Facebook Messenger: only recently added encryption after years of pressure.

Discord: no end-to-end encryption at all.

Instagram DMs: fully readable by Meta.

Most social apps stop at "we are on blockchain."

Dlicom is building its own blockchain layer.

That is a completely different level of ambition.

THE ZEEVE PARTNERSHIP

Dlicom has partnered with Zeeve, a leading Web3 infrastructure company, to launch a dedicated ZKSync L2 Hyperchain.

This is not an integration. This is not a plugin.

This is Dlicom building its own sovereign Layer 2 network on top of ZKSync technology.

WHAT IS A ZKSYNC HYPERCHAIN?

ZKSync Hyperchains are independent blockchains that inherit the security of Ethereum through zero-knowledge proofs.

ZK proofs are a form of cryptography that lets a system prove something is true without revealing any underlying data.

For a social and financial platform like Dlicom, this means transactions can be verified privately, instantly, and at near-zero cost.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR USERS

More capacity. The network can handle far more activity without slowing down.

More privacy. ZK technology keeps sensitive transaction data protected by default.

More efficiency. Lower costs across every interaction on the platform.

HOW THIS CONNECTS TO THE BIGGER PICTURE

Base handles the present. The ZKSync Hyperchain handles the future.

As Dlicom scales to millions of users, the infrastructure scales with it.

Most projects promise scalability. Dlicom is engineering it.

Code is law. And law needs to be verified.

WHO IS HACKEN?

Hacken is one of the most respected cybersecurity firms in the blockchain industry.

They have audited smart contracts for some of the biggest names in Web3 including Binance, Avalanche, Solana, and hundreds of DeFi protocols.

When Hacken signs off on a contract, the industry pays attention.

WHAT AN AUDIT ACTUALLY MEANS

A smart contract audit is a line-by-line review of the code that controls your funds.

Auditors look for vulnerabilities, logic errors, and attack vectors that could allow someone to drain wallets, manipulate token supply, or exploit the platform.

Without an audit, you are trusting code nobody independent has reviewed.

With a Hacken audit, you have verified proof that the code does exactly what it claims to do.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR A NEW USER

Dlicom's Hacken audit is a direct answer to that fear.

The contract has been reviewed. The code has been verified. The security has been tested by professionals whose entire reputation depends on getting it right.

→ controlling interaction
→ participating in network value creation

@DlicomApp places community at the center of the experience, recognizing that technology alone is rarely enough to sustain long-term ecosystems.
