The most valuable infrastructure in Web3 may not be the infrastructure people notice.

While attention is often directed toward blockchains, protocols, and financial systems, another layer quietly determines whether communities grow or struggle: communication.

Not communication as marketing.

Communication as infrastructure.

This is the lens through which I view Dlicom.

The crypto industry has solved many technical problems over the past decade. Transactions are faster. Networks are more efficient. Development tools are improving. Yet one challenge continues to affect nearly every ecosystem regardless of size.

Information remains fragmented.

Users jump between platforms searching for updates. Communities rely on multiple channels to stay informed. Important discussions happen in one place, while key announcements happen somewhere else.

As a result, information becomes available but not necessarily accessible.

There is a difference.

Accessible information is organized, discoverable, and connected. Available information simply exists somewhere on the internet.

Many projects achieve the second. Few achieve the first.

Dlicom appears to recognize this distinction.

Its broader direction suggests an effort to create stronger connections between communities, content, and communication channels. Rather than viewing each platform as an isolated destination, the focus seems to be on creating continuity across the entire user journey.

That continuity is becoming increasingly important.

As Web3 grows, projects are no longer competing only for attention. They are competing for comprehension.

The projects that users understand are the projects they trust.

The projects they trust are the projects they support.

And the projects they support are the ones that build lasting communities.

This is why I believe communication infrastructure deserves far more attention than it currently receives.

Without it, even strong products can struggle to explain their value. Communities can become disconnected. Valuable information can disappear beneath constant noise.

What stands out about Dlicom is that it is operating in a space many people underestimate. Communication is often viewed as a secondary function, something that comes after the technology is built.

In reality, communication is what connects technology to people.

Without that connection, innovation has limited impact.

My perspective is simple: the next stage of Web3 growth will not be driven solely by better technology. It will also be driven by better systems for sharing, organizing, and understanding information.

Dlicom’s direction aligns with that reality.

And as digital ecosystems become larger and more complex, the importance of that mission will only increase.
@DlicomApp

Most networks struggle when data packets are delayed or lost.

That’s where RLNC (Random Linear Network Coding) changes the game.

Instead of sending data in the traditional way, RLNC encodes information into multiple coded pieces, allowing nodes to recover the original data even if some packets never arrive.

The result?

🔹 Faster data propagation
🔹 Better bandwidth efficiency
🔹 Higher reliability
🔹 Lower latency for blockchain networks

This is one of the key innovations behind @get_optimum vision for scalable and real time Web3 infrastructure.

Smarter networking may be just as important as smarter blockchains.

Dlicom Community Guidelines: Establishing Standards for a Healthy Web3 Social Ecosystem

As Dlicom continues to grow as a leading Web3 SocialFi platform, maintaining high-quality, respectful, and productive community spaces remains one of our core priorities. Communities on Dlicom are designed to be more than simple discussion groups-they are sovereign, self-governed environments where users, creators, and builders can connect, collaborate, and thrive with full ownership. @DlicomApp

Key Features of Dlicom Communities

Public and Private Options
Communities can be open to all or restricted via invites and approvals.

Advanced Moderation Tools
Administrators benefit from powerful features including announcement-only channels, content removal capabilities, role management, and DAO-style governance through token-based voting.

Integrated Web3 Experience
Self-custody wallets, end-to-end encrypted messaging, and seamless creator monetization tools.

Encouraged Practices:

• Sharing original, creative, and value-driven content (text posts, DliClips, images, and discussions)
• Engaging in constructive dialogue and knowledge exchange
• Supporting creators through tipping and legitimate monetization
• Building meaningful connections and long-term reputation
• Responsible discussions around Web3 projects, technologies, and opportunities

Prohibited Conduct:

To ensure a safe and professional environment, the following are strictly not permitted:

• Harassment, bullying, discrimination, or hate speech
• Spam, unsolicited promotions, or low-value self-advertisement
• Scams, fraudulent schemes, phishing attempts, or misleading claims
• Adult, explicit, or otherwise inappropriate content
• Violations of privacy or disclosure of personal information
• Promotion of illegal activities or harmful misinformation

Note: Community administrators may establish additional specific rules tailored to their group's focus and standards. All members are expected to comply with both platform-wide and community-specific policies.

Moderation and Enforcement:
Administrators are empowered to maintain order within their communities. Violations should be reported promptly through the in-app tools. Persistent or severe breaches may result in content removal, warnings, or account suspension.

Our Collective Responsibility:
Dlicom aims to set a new standard in Web3 social platforms-one that balances decentralization with accountability. By adhering to these guidelines, we can foster spaces that are innovative, inclusive, and sustainable for all participants.

We invite community leaders to implement clear rules from the outset and members to contribute positively and responsibly. Together, we can build the most trusted and valuable social network in the Web3 space.

Thank you for being part of the Dlicom ecosystem.

Own Your Social.

Dlicom is not just another social media app it is a Web3-native SocialFi ecosystem where social interaction and financial participation exist together in one platform

Telegram built powerful communities, but monetization and on-chain ownership are still limited.
Dlicom is designed to change that model at the infrastructure level.
The platform combines:
• Short-form vertical video through DliClips

• Community-driven social spaces

• Native Web3 browser for dApp access
• On-chain tipping with any EVM-compatible token

Built on Base with low transaction fees, fixed token supply, audited smart contracts, integrated Web3 infrastructure, and a global-first approach, Dlicom aims to combine the strengths of Facebook, Instagram, and Telegram into a single decentralized ecosystem focused on ownership, participation, and real utility

from the way i see it, right now @DlicomApp is still early, and i mean very early.

the staking rewards may only become juicy if the app actually gets a lot of users and makes real revenue.

if it stays small, our earnings in the app may be tiny.

 creators earn when people buy or sell keys. it exploded then died hard. 

it was more like gambling on influencers than steady revenue share.

- farcaster / warpcast: 

this one was just decentralized twitter vibes. 

some earnings was through tokens like $degen, but not direct platform revenue sharing to stakers.

very few actually send real revenue (stablecoin) back to users like dlicom claims they do.

truth is, if you just wanna scroll and chat, then it may probably not be life changing for you.

but, if you believe Dlicom app will grow, then buy some $DLI cheap in presale, stake it long term, post content, bring in friends … who knows?

it’s still high risk, i know, because most web3 apps fail or go quiet.

but i want to think of it as betting on a new social app that actually tries to pay its users instead of just farming them.

so yes, to the team, i say kudos. you're doing a good job.

2065134501521437162.text:
i went through the whitepaper to check the @DlicomApp app explanation on what it is about, 

and i saw something good i didn't see in some other apps that tried to do this sort of thing. 

it was how everything i read just felt naturally put together instead of being forced.

check it out, if you haven't.

dlicom has shown that it is able to attain that height of being a mobile first app that mixes normal social stuff with real Web3 features without making it complicated. 

you get your regular feed, short videos called DliClips, communities, direct messages, and the ability to tip creators inside the app. 

hmm... its big.

they built in a real self custodial wallet from the moment you sign up. 

you control your own keys, no one else can touch your stuff, and it works across multiple EVM chains. 

what stood out to me was the DliClips part which i think dlicom community is using well, cos i see a lot of  videos

i like the redesigned version 2.1.0 though

it has better fullscreen, smoother playback, easier uploads, and background music. 

the main feed shows posts from people you follow and your communities. 

you can react with different emotions, and creators can see exactly who viewed and reacted to their content. 

messaging is end to end encrypted by default.

communities got proper moderation tools now too, like admins being able to lock posting or delete stuff when needed.

that was a big upgrade.

there’s also a built in web3 browser so you can jump into any dApp, sign transactions, and do everything without switching apps or using extensions. 

you can tip too. so tip me inside the app, ok? kek

@DlicomApp 's vision reflects this idea by placing communication, ownership, and community building at the center of the user experience. Rather than treating social interaction as an afterthought, the platform integrates it directly into the ecosystem alongside Web3 functionality.

📢Visuals are usually the first thing people notice. Not the text.

Think about the accounts you keep coming back to. Most of the time, something catches your eye before you even read a word. A frame, a meme, a color, a short clip. That first impression matters more than people think.

One thing that stood out from @DlicomApp latest article is that strong visuals are not about having a huge budget or being a professional designer.

What actually works is relevance.

Content that reflects what your audience feels right now will almost always perform better than something polished but empty. If people would send it to a friend or stop scrolling for a second, you're already moving in the right direction.

Another important point is simplicity.

Your visuals should work even as a tiny thumbnail. One clear focus, readable elements, strong contrast. That's often enough.

And creating content today is easier than ever. You don't need complicated tools. A good screenshot, a quick edit in Canva, a short CapCut clip, or even a simple vertical video can outperform something overdesigned if the idea is stronger.

Short-form content especially feels underrated. The first few seconds decide whether someone stays or scrolls.

At the end of the day, visuals shouldn't feel like decoration. They should feel like part of the conversation.

One thing I’ve noticed about most social apps is that they make crypto feel like an extra feature instead of a natural part of the experience.

You chat in one app, scroll content in another, and then open a wallet app every time you want to send or receive funds. It works, but it creates unnecessary friction.

That’s one of the biggest reasons many Web3 social platforms struggle to keep users engaged.

What makes seamless crypto integration so important is simple: people want convenience.

If sending crypto feels as easy as sending a message, adoption becomes much easier.

Instead of copying wallet addresses, switching between apps, and worrying about mistakes, users can interact, communicate, and transact in one place.

This is one of the ideas behind @DlicomApp. The platform combines a social network, instant messaging, and a self-custody crypto wallet into a single ecosystem.

Users can chat, engage with communities, create content, and even send cryptocurrency directly through conversations without leaving the app.

I think this matters because the future of SocialFi isn’t just about adding tokens to social media. 

It’s about making ownership, payments, and participation feel natural. When wallets, messaging, and content creation are connected, users spend less time dealing with technical barriers and more time actually using the platform.

Another benefit is creator monetization. Instead of relying only on traditional advertising models, creators can receive tips, rewards, and other forms of support directly inside the platform. 

That creates a more direct relationship between creators and their communities.

At the end of the day, the platforms that win in Web3 will probably be the ones that make crypto almost invisible.

Users shouldn’t have to think about wallets, gas fees, or complicated steps every few minutes. They should simply enjoy the app while crypto works smoothly in the background.

That’s what true seamless integration looks like, and it could be one of the biggest factors that drives mainstream adoption of social apps in the years ahead.

Bluesky, Farcaster, and Lens are now competing to build the future of social media through what many are calling the "social graph war."

Where it used to be about user numbers, it's now about ownership of identity and audience.

Some major changes are starting to emerge:

• Decentralized Identity
Digital identities are no longer dependent on a single platform.

• Portable Audience
Followers and communities can be carried over to other applications without having to start from scratch.

• Creator Monetization
Creators have more ways to generate revenue directly from their communities.

• Social Ownership
Users are beginning to have greater control over their data and social activity.

These changes suggest that the future of social media may no longer be about who owns the largest platform, but rather who gives users the most control.

This is where @DlicomApp  becomes relevant.
Dlicom is not just building a social platform, but also combining privacy, communication, wallets, and digital ownership within a single Web3 ecosystem.

If the Web2 era was built on followers,
Then the next era might be built on ownership.

2063919054835134648.text:
Web3 is no longer just about finance.

A growing number of organizations now see decentralized communication as critical infrastructure, especially in situations where traditional platforms can be restricted, censored, or disrupted.

Recent discussions around Web3 communication networks highlight three important ideas:

• Resilient Communication
Networks remain accessible even when centralized systems face outages or restrictions.

• Censorship-Resistant Coordination
Communities can organize and share information without relying on a single authority.

• Identity Continuity
Users keep control of their digital identity across different platforms and ecosystems.
This marks a major shift in how people view Web3.

It's no longer only about moving value.
It's also about preserving access to information, communication, and digital freedom.

That is why projects like Dlicom are interesting.

By combining private communication, decentralized principles, and user-owned digital identity, @DlicomApp  is positioning itself within a category that may become increasingly important in the years ahead.

The future of Web3 may be built as much on communication as it is on finance.

2064716717369012297.text:
Several countries, such as Australia, France, Denmark, Greece, and Spain, have begun pushing for restrictions and age verification for young social media users.

This is no longer a small discussion.
Governments are beginning to view social media design as a public health and safety issue.

The reasons are quite clear:

• Exposure to age-inappropriate content
• Doomscrolling and digital addiction
• Risk of data exploitation of young users
• Impact on mental health

These changes indicate that the era of completely unregulated social media is slowly coming to an end.

However, a new question arises:

How can we protect users without compromising their privacy?

Many current verification systems require more personal data, which creates new risks for users.
This is where the Web3 approach becomes interesting.

Concepts such as:

• User-owned identity
• Selective disclosure
• Privacy-preserving verification

have the potential to allow someone to prove their age or eligibility for access without having to reveal their entire identity.

The future of social media may not be just about user engagement and growth.

But it's also about finding a balance between:

Safety 🤝 Privacy

And that's the challenge that projects like Dlicom are trying to address.
#Dlicom 
@DlicomApp

2065099132071780375.text:
A new study suggests that AI can identify anonymous social media accounts by connecting small pieces of information scattered across different platforms.

In other words:

Being anonymous online is becoming harder than ever.

You may never reveal your real name.
You may never share your address.

Yet AI can still build a surprisingly accurate profile by analyzing patterns, posts, interactions, and digital footprints.

This highlights a growing challenge in the AI era:

Privacy is no longer just about what you share.

It's also about what can be inferred.

Key concerns include:

• Cross-platform identity tracking
• Behavioral profiling
• Data aggregation at scale
• Loss of digital anonymity

As AI becomes more powerful, traditional privacy assumptions may no longer be enough.
This is why conversations around:

• User-owned identity
• Data ownership
• Privacy-first platforms
• Digital sovereignty

are becoming increasingly important.

Projects like Dlicom are part of this broader discussion.

The goal is not simply to create another social platform, but to explore how users can regain more control over their identity, communication, and personal data.
The AI era may force us to rethink what privacy really means online.
#Dlicom

The European Union is marking 10 years of GDPR with a message that feels more relevant than ever:

Your data, your rights.

Over the past decade, GDPR has reshaped how companies collect, store, and use personal information.

The core idea is simple:

User data should not be treated as a company asset.

It should be treated as a user right.

This shift has influenced how businesses approach:

• Privacy
• Consent
• Transparency
• Data protection

And the trend is only getting stronger.
Around the world, regulators are increasingly pushing for greater user control and accountability from digital platforms.
What's interesting is that this aligns closely with many of the principles that Web3 has discussed for years:

• User ownership
• Self-sovereignty
• Privacy-first design
• Control over personal information

Data ownership is no longer a futuristic concept.

It's becoming an expectation.

Projects like Dlicom are building around this reality by exploring models where users have greater control over their identity, communication, and digital presence.
The future of the internet may not belong to platforms that collect the most data.
It may belong to platforms that give users the most control over it.
